official.deadline_note: The portfolio page publishes no single deadline: it states that the call for applications for grants for students experiencing difficulties is usually published in September, and that scholarships and awards are granted throughout the year. Each individual call sets its own binding deadline. The total merit-based exemption for first-year second cycle students is granted automatically at enrolment to those who already hold a Bachelor's degree obtained by 31 July 2026, or by 30 November 2026 for healthcare professional degree programmes.
official.application_cycle: Rolling portfolio of calls published throughout the academic year
official.status_note: The study grants and subsidies page is live and presents the benefits available at every stage of study, directing students to the University notice board at bandi.unibo.it for the current open calls.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The portfolio includes tuition fee reductions based on financial situation or merit offered by the Region of Emilia Romagna (ERGO), a total merit-based fee exemption for first-year second cycle degree students, and full exemption from tuition fees for ER.GO scholarship recipients.
benefits: Fee exemptions and reductions according to your economic situation, offered by the Region of Emilia Romagna (ERGO)
Total merit-based exemption from enrolment fees for students in the first year of a second cycle degree programme who graduated on time and with top marks
Full exemption from tuition fees and refund of the regional tax for ER.GO study grant recipients
ER.GO study grants, with amounts diversified by ISEE band and by student status as in sede, pendolare or fuori sede
A 20% fee reduction for students with other family members attending university
Accommodation in the university halls of residence in the Region and grants covering part of the cost of rent
Discounted university canteen meals and special prices for public transport passes in Bologna, Cesena, Forli, Ravenna and Rimini
Free licences for Matlab, Prezi, Stata Se, Microsoft 365 and Mathematica
Reduced conventions with cinemas, museums, theatres and sport matches
150-hour student collaboration grants and peer tutoring grants
eligibility: Enrolled at the University of Bologna on a degree programme
Financial situation or merit, as assessed under the relevant ERGO or ER.GO scheme

For the total merit-based exemption in the first year of a second cycle degree programme: the first cycle degree obtained during a.y. 2025/26 at the University of Bologna by 31 July 2026, within the course's established duration, with a degree mark of no less than 110/110 (30 November 2026 for healthcare professional degree programmes)
Personal, family or economic difficulty, for grants aimed at students experiencing difficulties
Certification of a civil disability percentage of 66% or more and certification under Law 104/92, for fee exemption
A parent receiving a disability pension under Law 118/1971, for fee exemption
Becoming a mother or father during the academic year, for fee exemption
Permanent membership of a religious order with entire support from it for living expenses, for a tax exemption
Citizenship in a listed particularly poor or developing country, or in a non-EU non-OECD country, for the reduced fixed fee
International protection status, for the MUR and Ministry of the Interior schemes
Nationality or residence abroad, for MAECI scholarships for international students
Personal circumstances, for scholarships for students from countries where access to university is prevented or severely limited
requirements: For the reduced fixed fee: citizenship in a listed country, enrolment for a number of years equal to or less than the standard duration of the degree programme increased by one year, and family income and/or assets only outside Italy

For the reduced fixed fee: submit the form on the ER.GO portal declaring the requirements and accepting the flat-rate fee, or reply to the email from the Student Contributions Office confirming that family income and assets are solely based abroad
The reduced fixed fee and the total or partial exemption based on economic status are incompatible - applicants must choose one
The total merit-based exemption is incompatible with other merit-based benefits granted by the University
For ER.GO benefits: apply every academic year, with the deadlines in the call for applications binding and non-extendable
documents: Documents specified by each individual call and by ERGO or ER.GO for the relevant benefit
For the reduced fixed fee, a declaration on the family's economic situation without certificates, submitted through the ER.GO portal
Certification of a civil disability percentage of 66% or more and certification under Law 104/92, for the disability exemption
Documentation of the family's income and assets only outside Italy, if applying for the economic-status exemption instead of the flat-rate fee
selection_criteria: Fee reductions based on financial situation are assessed on the family's economic status under the ERGO scheme
ER.GO study grant amounts are diversified by the ISEE band of the family and by the student's status as in sede, pendolare or fuori sede

The total merit-based exemption is granted automatically at enrolment to those who already hold a qualifying Bachelor's degree; applicants who are entitled but not granted it automatically should contact the Student Administration Office
coverage: Reduction in tuition fees based on financial situation or merit

Total merit-based exemption from enrolment fees for first-year second cycle degree students, leaving only EUR 157.04 payable (regional right to higher education tax of EUR 140, EUR 16 stamp duty and EUR 1.04 accident insurance premium)
Full exemption from university tuition fees and refund of the regional tax for ER.GO study grant recipients

Reduced fixed fee for citizens of particularly poor and developing countries for a.y. 2026/27: EUR 500 + EUR 157.04 for first or single cycle programmes, EUR 600 + EUR 157.04 for second cycle programmes where the student is a freshman or has the minimum credits; EUR 600 + EUR 157.04 and EUR 700 + EUR 157.04 respectively where the minimum credits are not held
Reduced fixed fee for nationals of non-OECD countries for a.y. 2026/27: EUR 1,000 + EUR 157.04, EUR 1,200 + EUR 157.04, EUR 1,200 + EUR 157.04 and EUR 1,400 + EUR 157.04 on the same conditions
Accommodation in university halls of residence in the Region, and grants covering part of the cost of rent
Discounted canteen meals and public transport, free software licences and cultural price reductions
application_method: Check the University notice board at bandi.unibo.it for the current open calls in each benefit category
For fee reductions and ER.GO benefits, apply through the ER.GO online portal and declare the family's economic status
For the reduced fixed fee without claiming other benefits, complete the personal data section and the reduced fixed fee form on the ER.GO portal and accept the flat-rate fee
For the reduced fixed fee together with ER.GO and Unibo benefits, complete the ER.GO portal form and also declare that the economic status should be submitted for benefits
For the total merit-based exemption, no application is needed where it is granted automatically at enrolment; otherwise contact the Student Administration Office
official.application_route: Identify the benefit you qualify for on the study grants and subsidies page, then apply through the ER.GO online portal or the individual call published on bandi.unibo.it.
official.citizenship_residency: Most fee reductions and grants depend on the family's economic situation as assessed by ERGO and are open to enrolled students regardless of nationality. The reduced fixed fee is restricted to citizens of listed particularly poor or developing countries or non-EU non-OECD countries whose family has income and/or assets only outside Italy. International protection holders, refugees and students from conflict-affected countries have dedicated routes.
official.international_eligibility: Open to international students. Dedicated routes exist for citizens of particularly poor and developing countries and non-OECD countries (reduced fixed fee), asylum seekers and refugees (Unibo for Refugees, MUR-CRUI and Ministry of the Interior schemes), international students (MAECI scholarships), and students from countries where access to university is prevented or severely limited.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The portfolio is administered across different bodies: ERGO and ER.GO for regional fee reductions, accommodation and study grants; the Ministry of Universities and Research and the Ministry of the Interior with CRUI for international protection holders; and the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI) for its scholarships.
official.duration: Duration of the study programme; benefits are applied per academic year
official.description: The University of Bologna's study grants and subsidies portfolio is presented as financial support at every stage of study, combining regional tuition fee reductions and exemptions based on financial situation or merit, ERGO and ER.GO grants, accommodation and rent support, and dedicated routes for international students, refugees and students from conflict-affected countries, alongside signposting to national schemes run by the Ministry of Universities and Research, the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
official.program_type: University study grants and fee subsidy portfolio

verification.notes: Read the study grants and subsidies portfolio page, the total merit-based exemption page and the reduced fixed fee page on unibo.it. Confirmed the merit exemption conditions and the EUR 157.04 residual payment, the a.y. 2026/27 reduced fixed fee amounts, the 20% sibling reduction, the ERGO/ER.GO administration split and the absence of any published award figure for the portfolio. Reviewed the ER.GO study grant page, which is in Italian and sets amounts per call.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a portfolio rather than a single award, so the useful question is not which scholarship to apply for but which benefit you already qualify for: several of them, including the total merit-based fee exemption for first-year second cycle students and the reduced fixed fee for citizens of listed poor, developing or non-OECD countries, are applied through ER.GO rather than through a scholarship competition. The single highest-value item for most international students is the reduced fixed fee, which caps the fee at EUR 500 to EUR 1,400 plus the always-payable EUR 157.04 first instalment instead of the maximum programme contribution. Note that the flat-rate fee and the economic-status exemption are mutually exclusive, so choosing one closes the other, and the family must have income and assets only outside Italy to take the flat rate.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Bologna students with a low family economic status, first-year second cycle students who graduated on time with top marks, and international students from listed poor, developing or non-OECD countries whose family income sits entirely abroad.
application_readiness_checklist: Work out which track suits you - flat-rate fee or economic-status exemption - because they are incompatible and the choice must be made on the ER.GO form
Confirm your country appears on the published list of particularly poor or developing countries, or of non-OECD countries, before relying on the reduced fixed fee

If you are entering a second cycle degree from a Unibo first cycle degree, check whether you graduated by 31 July 2026 within the standard duration with at least 110/110, since the exemption is then automatic
Confirm your credit position: the minimum credits run from 11 August 2025 to 10 August 2026 and are 10 credits to enter year two and 25 credits to enter years after the second
Budget for the EUR 157.04 first instalment in every scenario, including full exemption, since it is never waived
Check bandi.unibo.it rather than this page for live calls, since each benefit has its own deadline
common_rejection_risks: Claiming both the reduced fixed fee and the economic-status exemption, which are incompatible and will force you back to the maximum fee
Assuming the flat-rate fee is automatic and then missing the Student Contributions Office confirmation email, which leaves you charged the maximum tuition
Submitting foreign income documentation that is incomplete or incorrect, which ER.GO checks thoroughly and which can lead to benefits being revoked
Having family income or assets inside Italy, which removes eligibility for the flat-rate fee entirely
Exceeding the standard programme duration plus one year, which removes eligibility for the reduced fixed fee
Missing a benefit call deadline, which the portfolio states are binding and non-extendable
Claiming the merit exemption alongside another merit-based University benefit, which is not permitted
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything the fee reductions do not touch: living costs, accommodation unless a hall of residence place or rent grant is awarded, travel, and the residual fee. Students on the reduced fixed fee pay EUR 500 to EUR 1,400 plus EUR 157.04, and even fully exempt students still pay EUR 157.04, which comprises the regional tax of EUR 140, EUR 16 stamp duty and EUR 1.04 accident insurance.
document_audit: For the flat-rate fee you submit a declaration without certificates, but if you instead claim the economic-status exemption you must produce full documentation of income and assets held only outside Italy
Disability exemptions need both the certification of a civil disability percentage of 66% or more and certification under Law 104/92
Dual-nationality applicants must specify where the family holds income and assets, and may only accept the flat rate if those are exclusively in a particularly poor or non-OECD country
Since ER.GO revokes benefits where documentation has missing or incorrect data, keep the evidence trail for any declaration you make
alerts: The reduced fixed fee figures quoted are for academic year 2026/27 and will change in later years
The total merit-based exemption applies only to students who obtained their first cycle degree at the University of Bologna itself - external graduates are not covered
Grants for students experiencing difficulties typically open in September, so set a reminder for early autumn rather than waiting for an announcement
The Ireland-Palestine route, MUR-CRUI and Ministry of the Interior schemes are separate competitions with their own administrators and should not be conflated with the University's own portfolio
Authentication for ER.GO benefits runs through the ER.GO portal, and the process must be repeated every academic year even without prior university enrolment
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Identify the benefit, then apply through the ER.GO online portal for fee and grant benefits or through the individual call on bandi.unibo.it, with the merit exemption granted automatically at enrolment where the degree conditions are met.
